html:
São Tomé, an uninhabited island in the Gulf of Guinea found by Portuguese sailors around 1470, was settled from 1493 and became the first big sugar plantation colony worked by enslaved Africans.

The first settlers included convicts and about two thousand Jewish children taken from their parents in Portugal. Enslaved people were brought from the mainland, from Benin and Kongo, to clear forest and work the cane, and the island became a depot of the Atlantic slave trade.

By the mid 1500s it was one of the world's main sources of sugar. Revolts such as Amador's, raids and competition from Brazil ended the boom by about 1600, but the system of mill, plantation and slave labour it tested shaped the Americas.
sum: São Tomé, an uninhabited island in the Gulf of Guinea found by Portuguese sailors around 1470, was settled from 1493 and became the first big sugar plantation colony worked by enslaved Africans.
